reason: The flora says the stems are brown at the base ('basally brown and peeled off'). Stem base + color brown says exactly that.
10–50(–80) dm converts correctly to 100–500 cm with an outer maximum of 800 cm. This is the height of shrubs or trees, so whole plant + height fits.

fix: 'exerted' is a misspelling of 'exserted' and should be read as exserted (PATO_0000623).
reason: The pistil has 2–4 exserted styles, so style + exserted is right.

fix: 'axiUary' is an OCR error for 'axillary'. Read it as the axillary value, not as bare position.
reason: The flora says the sporophyte is axillary near the base. Whole plant is an acceptable bearer because 'sporophyte' is one of its synonyms. But giving only the general quality 'position' drops the value the flora states, and FLOPO_0991000 axillary already exists.
The peduncle is 'glabrous to pubescent'. Pilosity with a glabrous-to-pubescent range is right.
'Bracteoles equaling bracts' is a comparison of size, normally read as length. A ratio of 1 to the bracts is right.
'Stemless' (acaulescent) means the stem is absent, so stem + present, negated, is right.
The petiole is 1–1.5 cm long.

fix: 'not glaucous' denies the waxy bloom (glaucous). It does not mean the stem is not green. Map 'not glaucous' to glaucous, negated, with no color value and no 'approximately' qualifier.
reason: The annotation says the stem is not (approximately) green, which the flora does not say. The flora only says the stems lack a glaucous bloom.

fix: In '..., the tip broadly rounded' the shape belongs to the apex of the part being described, not to the whole part.
reason: The flora says the leaf tip is rounded, not the whole leaf. Obtuse/rounded is acceptable as the quality, but the bearer should be the leaf apex.
'Lateral united petals ± clawed' means the petals are more or less clawed. Petal + clawed + approximately is right.
The leaf blade length is 1–2 cm, with outer extremes of 0.5 and 2.5 cm. Correct.
The primary inflorescence branches are 1–2 mm long in fruit. Higher order inflorescence axis (synonym: inflorescence branch) with the fruit development stage is right.
The stamens are shorter than the petals. Correct.
The legume is unarmed, meaning the fruit has no spines. Spiny, negated, is right.
The blade is occasionally ovate to obovate. Leaf lamina + shape with a range from ovate to obovate and the 'occasionally' qualifier is right.

target: from_value: oblong-lanceolate (a compound shape: oblong and lanceolate, or a FLOPO compound value if one exists), not oblong (PATO_0000946)
fix: In a hyphenated shape 'X-Y', Y is the main shape and X modifies it. It must not be cut down to its first part alone.
reason: 'oblong-lanceolate' was mapped to plain oblong (PATO_0000946). This loses 'lanceolate' and changes the meaning. The second alternative, narrowly lanceolate, is right.

fix: The narrower bearer wing petal (PO_0025325) would be better.
reason: 'Wing shorter than keel': the wing is a petal, and the comparison target keel (PO_0025327) is right. Petal as bearer is broad but still true.
The leaves are 'minutely pubescent above, tomentose below'. Tomentose on the lower (abaxial) side of the leaf is right.
'Margins spinulose' means the margin has small spines. Leaf lamina margin + spiny is acceptable.

fix: In '<color> <hair adjective>' (e.g. 'brown hirtellous') the color belongs to the hairs, not to the part that carries them.
reason: The brown or gray-brown color describes the hirtellous hairs on the branchlets and petiole, not the branch surface itself.
The leaves are 3–12 × 0.7–2 cm, so the width is 0.7–2 cm. Correct.
The dorsal sepal is 3-veined. Three veins (vascular bundles) within the sepal is right.

target: fine roots (no PO class), or rejected as a single-site observation
fix: Absence of a qualified subset ('fine roots') must not be turned into absence of the whole part. Study observations in FEIS ('were absent' at one site) are not taxon traits.
reason: The annotation says the plant has no roots. The source reports roots and only says fine roots were absent in one excavated tree.
There are 2–10 capitula per corymb. A count of capitula within the inflorescence is right.
'Erect herb or subshrubby herb' means herbaceous or suffrutescent habit, as given.
The scape bracts are ample (large, over 15 cm). Bract + increased size is right.
The styles are connate nearly to the apex, so style + connate is true. The extent ('nearly to apex') is not recorded, but the statement still holds.
Male flowers have 4 stamens. Cliffortia is dioecious, so only male flowers have stamens and the count stays true without the 'male flowers' context.
The bract apex is acuminate. Correct.
